edits.reason: the baseline copies the three input regions into fixed rows (the largest region is 8 * 0x240 bytes) instead of three `Vec`s allocated inside a hook
the first 64 differences are kept in a fixed list (same JSON), not a `Vec` collected inside a hook

`input_snapshot` fills the fixed rows and `compare` reads the live regions in place (same hashes, changed-byte count and first 64 differences; the fork copied the live regions a second time, so a byte changing between the hash and the walk can now show in one and not the other, which a private qualification diagnostic tolerates)
the trace lives in fixed-capacity lists (same 192 events, 4 input checks, same JSON): the `Vec`s grew inside game hooks (review R5, lead ruling 3 of 2026-11-02)
a new session's trace allocated 192 events inside the request hook; the fixed list does not allocate

every editor event cloned the whole trace into a `Box` inside the hook and queued a write of it; now the newest trace replaces an unwritten older one in a fixed slot that the writer thread takes (lead ruling 2 and 3 of 2026-11-02)
the write reports its result to the writer thread, which keeps the state for the next turn on a failure

the trace file is written transactionally (temporary file, sync, replace; the old file stays on a failure) instead of `std::fs::write` over the live file (review R1); host tests in `engine::lobby::trace_slot` cover two loads and a failed write; offered back to the fork's fix ledger

stream/stack: Trace is Copy so the trace writer's BoxedSlot copies it into a boot-made heap buffer in place (moved by value it gave tr-trace-writer a 59,712 B frame on a 64 KiB stack: the Eden s4-07/u4b-02 boot fault)
stream/stack: Trace::EMPTY, the template the writer slot's two heap buffers are made from at init
